summary: One-line change computes the square-free norm on the original polynomial F instead of the square-free part f, which correctly recovers the factor that was being dropped over algebraic extensions; this matches the real upstream fix and resolves the reported issue. Mergeable as a minimal, targeted correctness fix.

issues.description: dmp_sqf_norm now receives F (the original, possibly non-square-free) rather than the square-free part f. Its shift loop searches for a square-free norm; a non-square-free input could change termination/iteration behavior or cost. The reported case z=(x-1)*(y-1) is already square-free so it is unaffected, but inputs with repeated factors over an extension (e.g. (x-1)**2*(y-1)) should be confirmed not to regress. Tests pass, so not blocking, but worth a covering test.

The fix likely works around incorrect behavior of multivariate dmp_sqf_part (which appears to drop the y-1 factor) rather than addressing that root cause directly. Computing the norm on F is itself legitimate (multiplicities are recovered later via dmp_trial_division), but the underlying sqf_part discrepancy may still surface in other code paths.

No comment explains why the norm is intentionally computed on F while f (the square-free part) is still kept for the len(factors)==1 branch. The f-vs-F distinction is subtle and a short comment would prevent a future maintainer from 'simplifying' it back to f.
